Field.name: InputFile
Field.manpage: Input model file. If this option is not entered, the first non-option argument will be used for the input file.

Field.name: OutputFile
Field.manpage: Output text file for points. If this option is not entered, the second non-option argument will be used for the output file.

Field.name: FloatingPoint
Field.usage: Output model coordinates as floating point, not integer
Field.manpage: Output model coordinates as floating point; otherwise the nearest integer value is output. Floating point output is the default unless the environment variable MODEL2POINT_INTEGERS is set to any value. This entry is still useful for overriding the environment variable setting.

Field.name: IntegerOutput
Field.usage: Output model coordinates as integer, not floating point
Field.manpage: Output model coordinates by taking the nearest integer instead of outputting floating point numbers, which is the default behavior. This option cannot be entered with \fB-float\fR.

Field.name: ScaledCoordinates
Field.usage: Output coordinates in model coordinate system, not as pixel indices
Field.manpage: Output coordinates in the model coordinate system, scaled by the original image pixel size in Angstroms and offset by origin values. The default is to output index coordinates corresponding to the pixel coordinates in the image.

Field.name: ObjectAndContour
Field.usage: Output object and contour numbers for each point (numbered from 1)

Field.name: Contour
Field.usage: Output contour number for each point (numbered from 1)

Field.name: NumberedFromZero
Field.usage: Output object and contour numbers starting from 0 instead of 1

Field.name: ZCoordinatesFromZero
Field.usage: Output Z coordinates starting from 0 instead of -0.5
Field.manpage: Output Z coordinates that are 0 instead of -0.5 at the bottom of the volume. In IMOD models, integer Z values are defined as being located in the middle of a pixel in Z, which makes model coordinates range from -0.5 to NZ - 0.5 for a volume of NZ slices. With this option, the point coordinates will be shifted so that they range from 0 to NZ, i.e., so that their fractional parts actually correspond to their fractional positions within the pixels in Z.

Field.name: PointSizes
Field.usage: Output point size after the Z coordinate on each line
Field.manpage: Output the point sizes for individual points, placing them after the Z coordinate on each line. If a point has no non-default size defined, or a contour has no point sizes for any of its points, then the 3D sphere size of the object will be used.

Field.name: TimesForContours
Field.usage: Output a time index on the first point of each contour
Field.manpage: Output a time index for each contour, on the first line for that contour. This index will appear after the Z coordinate, or after the point size if any, and before a contour or point value. If there are no time indexes, 0 will be output.

Field.name: ValuesInLastColumn
Field.usage: 1 or -1 to output point or contour value as last number on line
Field.manpage: Enter 1 to output general point values as the last number on each line, after the Z coordinate, or -1 to output general contour values for the first point in each contour. A point file with either format can be read back in by Point2model(1), provided that the -values option is given to that program. When a point or contour has no stored value, a value of 0 will be output, unless a different value is specified with the -fill option.

Field.name: FillValue
Field.usage: Value to output when contour/point has no stored value (default 0)

Field.name: MeshVertexCoordinates
Field.usage: Output mesh vertices for objects with no contours (1) or all objects (2)
Field.manpage: Output mesh vertex coordinates instead of contours points; enter 1 for output only from objects with no contours, or 2 for output from all objects with meshes. Output will be floating point regardless of whether the \fB-integer\fR option is entered or MODEL2POINT_INTEGERS is set. Use the \fB-object\fR option to output object numbers before the coordinates. The output is also affected by the \fB-zero\fR and \fB-zcoord\fR options.
